borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting, design, bulk and mass would be an undesirable addition to the dwelling. The proposal would cause undue harm to the character of the host dwelling and prevailing form of development. The excessive depth of the proposed rear extension in combination with the retention of the existing outbuilding would result in the rear amenity area of the dwelling appearing as overdeveloped and would result in a significant loss of amenity. The proposal is therefore contrary to the following policies which seek to ensure that development recognises local character and promotes good design: - National Planning Policy Framework National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, 2024)- Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)- The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)- Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD6 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037: (September 2024)

The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting and design would cause severe harm to the neighbouring occupiers.  The proposed development would introduce a significant level of overbearing and overshadowing to the site, with the site appearing as overdeveloped, failing to mitigate any significant impact to the amenity of neighbouring dwellings. The proposed development therefore constitutes unneighbourly development and is contrary to: - National Planning Policy Framework National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, 2024)- Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021);- The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012);- Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD6 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037: (September 2024)
description: Retrospective application for the construction of a single storey rear extension to provide habitable accommodation for the disabled occupant
